beats.words: Junior hiring at Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, has fallen off a cliff.
beats.point: The hook: the company that makes the AI is itself hiring far fewer juniors

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.motion: still; the label types in on "fallen off a cliff"

beats.words: So who trains the seniors you'll need in 2030?
beats.point: The question the piece answers, set on the object the whole piece uses

picture.what: The Ladder appears, drawn in cream line on the ink desk; the top rung lights with 2030, the bottom rung is drawn last and faint

beats.motion: rungs draw bottom to top; 2030 lands on "2030"

beats.words: I've been reading Anthropic's study of its own staff. It matters if you hire, so let me break it down.
beats.point: This comes from Anthropic's own report on its own staff, not a rumour

picture.what: The report's cover, "How Employment is Changing at Anthropic", The Anthropic Institute

beats.motion: slow push into the title

beats.words: One number stopped me. In early 2025, about one in four of its new technical hires were juniors.
beats.point: Early 2025: one in four new technical hires was a junior

picture.what: The bottom rung holds four hire marks, one of them butter-underlined: the junior

beats.motion: the four marks arrive on "one in four"

beats.words: Now it's fewer than one in ten, 27% down to 9%.
beats.point: The big moment: the junior share of hires fell from 27% to 9%

picture.what: The bottom rung's number counts down 27 to 9 in one second and the rung thins to a hairline

beats.motion: the count starts on "27%" and lands on "9%"; the piece's big moment

beats.words: Why? By August, its AI agents, which work on tasks by themselves, were putting in far more hours than its people.
beats.point: Why: by August AI agents were working six times the hours of the staff

picture.what: Two bars side by side, staff hours and agent hours; the agent bar grows to six times the staff bar

beats.motion: the agent bar grows on "far more hours"

beats.words: And many of its managers say AI is why they're hiring less.
beats.point: The managers say it out loud: AI is why they hire less

picture.what: The report's line "Around a third of ML and a fifth of SWE managers reported hiring less due to AI", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps on "hiring less"

beats.words: So when AI writes the first draft, there's less first-draft work to give a junior.
beats.point: The mechanism in one sentence: the first draft was the junior's work

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: And Anthropic isn't alone. A study of US firms found the same thing.
beats.point: It is not only Anthropic: a study of US firms finds the same

picture.what: The study's page, "Generative AI as Seniority-Biased Technological Change", Stanford Digital Economy Lab

beats.motion: slow push into the title

beats.words: Where companies brought in AI, junior jobs dropped while senior jobs kept growing.
beats.point: Where firms adopt AI, junior jobs fall while senior jobs keep rising

picture.what: Two lines from 2023: senior employment keeps rising, junior employment turns down; no numbers on the axis, only the direction the study reports

beats.motion: the two lines part on "while senior jobs kept growing"

beats.words: It happened through slower hiring. Fewer juniors got taken on in the first place.
beats.point: It happens through hires that never happen, not layoffs

picture.what: The study's line "The junior decline is driven primarily by slower hiring rather than increased separations", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps on "slower hiring"

beats.words: Now, before anyone panics, we've been here before. Twice.
beats.point: The turn: this has happened before, twice

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.motion: the label lands on "Twice"

beats.words: You'd think cash machines would have finished off bank tellers. In America, an average city branch went from needing 20 tellers to 13.
beats.point: Cash machines cut the tellers a city branch needed from 20 to 13

picture.what: A branch drawn as 20 teller marks; seven fade, 13 remain

beats.motion: marks fade on "20 tellers to 13"

beats.words: But banks used the savings to open more branches. In cities, there were 43% more branches.
beats.point: Banks spent the savings on more branches: 43% more in cities

picture.what: The branch copies itself across the desk until there are 43% more

beats.motion: copies appear on "more branches", the number on "43%"

beats.words: So teller jobs held up. And tellers spent less time counting cash and more time with customers.
beats.point: The teller job held up and changed: less cash, more people

picture.what: The IMF article's line "cash handling became less important and human interaction more important", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps on "more time with customers"

beats.words: Then came spreadsheets. Since 1980, about 400,000 bookkeeping clerk jobs have gone. But 600,000 accountant jobs have been added.
beats.point: Spreadsheets took 400,000 clerk jobs and added 600,000 accountant jobs

picture.what: 400,000 clerk marks fall away; 600,000 accountant marks stack up above them, taller

beats.motion: the fall on "have gone", the stack on "added"

beats.words: That's because accounting got cheaper, so people bought more of it.
beats.point: Why the jobs grew back: cheaper work, more of it bought

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: So each time, a tool took the dull bottom of a job, and the job that was left got bigger.
beats.point: The pattern: the tool takes the bottom, the job grows taller

picture.what: Both scenes fold back into the Ladder, now taller than at the start, a new rung added at the top

beats.motion: the ladder grows on "got bigger"

beats.words: Here's what worries me this time.
beats.point: His turn to what worries him this time

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Back then, there was still a first step on the career ladder. Tellers moved to the customer side, and there were more accountant jobs to start in.
beats.point: Back then the bottom rung was still there to start on

picture.what: The taller Ladder, its bottom rung solid, marked TELLER and CLERK in Plex Mono as the two starting jobs

beats.motion: the bottom rung brightens on "first step"

beats.words: This time, AI takes the first draft itself, the very work juniors learned on.
beats.point: This time the bottom rung itself goes: the first draft was the learning

picture.what: The Ladder with no bottom rung: the camera rests on the gap. The frame the cover and thumbnail echo

beats.motion: the bottom rung lifts away on "first draft itself"; hold

beats.words: Anthropic's own report says staff in some roles are moving away from the hands-on work that built their skills.
beats.point: Anthropic's report says so itself

picture.what: The report's line "In some roles, they are increasingly removed from the object-level work that originally built their skills", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps on "hands-on work"

beats.words: And I reckon juniors feel that most.
beats.point: His read: juniors feel this most, said as his

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: And the cut is quiet, because no one gets a redundancy letter. It hits the people who never get hired, so they never show up in anyone's numbers.
beats.point: The cut is invisible: it lands on people never hired

picture.what: The report's line "Employment protections for incumbents will not benefit those not hired to begin with", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps on "never get hired"

beats.words: Hiring managers at Anthropic now focus more and more on judgement. And that makes sense. If AI writes the first draft, you need people who can tell good work from bad.
beats.point: What managers want now is judgement

picture.what: The report's line "Hiring managers increasingly emphasize applicants' autonomy and judgment relative to specific technical expertise", highlighted

beats.motion: highlight sweeps on "judgement"

beats.words: But where did people learn judgement? In their junior years, doing the dull work, getting it wrong and being put right.
beats.point: Judgement is learned in the junior years

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Take away the junior years, and you still need the judgement. You just have nowhere left to grow it.
beats.point: Take away the junior rung and judgement has nowhere to grow

picture.what: The Ladder with its gap; JUDGEMENT sits on a high rung with nothing beneath it to climb from

beats.motion: the word lands on "judgement"; hold on the gap

beats.words: So I think this is every company's problem, and Anthropic is just early to it.
beats.point: This is every company's problem, and Anthropic is only early

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Anthropic's staff expect AI to do 75% of their own work by 2030.
beats.point: Anthropic's staff expect AI to do 75% of their work by 2030, against 28% for other Americans

picture.what: Two numbers, 75% for Anthropic staff and 28% for other Americans, as of August

beats.motion: 75% lands on "75%"; 28% follows

beats.words: However much AI does for you, you'll still need seniors to judge its work. And your 2030 seniors are juniors somewhere today. If no one hires them, no one trains them.
beats.point: Your 2030 seniors are today's juniors: no hire, no training

picture.what: The Ladder's top rung lights mint with 2030; a line runs from it down to the gap where the junior rung was

beats.motion: the line runs down on "juniors somewhere today"

beats.words: Here's why this one matters to me. In 2008, I was a junior at Microsoft. Yes, the people who make Excel.
beats.point: The dull job, told about a new hire (in both takes he tells it as "picture a new hire given a dull job", not as his own)

picture.what: A new hire's desk drawn on the ink desk: one spreadsheet open, the same task waiting row after row. No company logo, no year, no name

beats.motion: the sheet opens on "a new hire"

beats.words: I was asked to change the format of a spreadsheet with half a million rows, by hand. Same clicks, over and over.
beats.point: The same task by hand, for weeks

picture.what: The sheet's rows scroll while the same click repeats; a week counter ticks past week 1, 2, 3

beats.motion: the counter ticks on "weeks and weeks"

beats.words: I had a hunch it wasn't meant to be done that way, so I looked online. I found Excel macros, which record what you do so the computer repeats it.
beats.point: They spot the repeat and go looking for a better way

picture.what: The same sheet: one recorded action now repeats itself down the rows; the first two tries stop part way, the third runs to the end

beats.motion: the tries fail on "the first attempt doesn't work" and "neither does the second"

beats.words: Getting mine to work took me a few days, and I knew I might be wasting them.
beats.point: It was a risk: days that might be wasted

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: Then three weeks of work became a few hours.
beats.point: Weeks of work shrink to a few hours

picture.what: The week counter collapses to a few hours on one day

beats.motion: the collapse on "shrink to a few hours"

beats.words: And the real lesson was bigger than the macro. I learned to spot the boring job that repeats. And to stick with the fix when it doesn't work at first. I only learned that because someone gave me the dull job.
beats.point: The lesson is the habit, and the dull job is where it forms

picture.what: him to camera, his portrait in the full-height column, room treated (darkened and softened behind him)

beats.words: So here are two questions for your next hiring meeting, before you cut a junior role. Who on this team will be a senior in 2030? And what are they learning on today?

And when you find a boring job that repeats, learn how it works before you hand it to AI. Then build the fix, like my macro.

Every spoken word heard continuously: no chopped syllable at any join (audio compared around each edit boundary)
Every picture lands on the words it proves, framing centred, logos at equal size, no shake left in
Brand matches the reference frame: wordmark, captions, palette and the intro sting
Fact, transport and editorial status reported separately; ready only when all three pass
